citations.claim: total energy jumps ~4.8x in the collision step, far above the allowed bound
energy one step before is normal and near initial energy, so injection happens in step 8->9
heavy body speed nearly triples across the collision step while light body speed barely drops, inconsistent with elastic exchange

counterfactual.change: Changed bodies[0].e from 0.9 to 0 (single field); collision becomes fully inelastic so restitution impulse path is not exercised and no energy is created.

explanation: No-controller two-circle collision creates energy. At step 8 bodies are separate with normal energy ~3125 J; at step 9 they are in contact (gap ~0.047) and energy is ~14969 J. The heavy body (m=6.72) accelerates 22.8->64.3 m/s while the light body only slows 46.6->40.5 m/s, so net kinetic energy grows ~4.8x with zero controller work. Setting body 0 restitution to 0 removes the gain. Likely cause: restitution impulse for unequal masses uses wrong effective mass / restitution combination (e.g. applies full e-separation impulse without momentum-consistent scaling, or adds positional-correction velocity), injecting energy when a light elastic body strikes a much heavier one at high relative speed with substepped contact (40-42 substeps).
vision_note: The small and large circles approach each other across steps 6 to 8 and make contact at step 9. No walls, ejection, or overlap explosion is visible; the only event is the two-body touchdown exactly at the violating step.
